meta_title: Area of Ellipse x2/4 + y2/9 = 1 | NCERT Ex 8.1 Q5
meta_desc: Solved NCERT Class 12 Ex 8.1 Q5: area bounded by the ellipse x2/4 + y2/9 = 1 using integration. Try a free 8-question area MCQ quiz and check your steps.

quiz.title: Area Using Integration Quiz (Ellipses & Curves)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on finding area with definite integrals — ellipses, curves and standard regions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Application of Integrals: area of an ellipse and area under curves

questions.q: What is the total area enclosed by the ellipse x²/4 + y²/9 = 1?
questions.explanation: Here a² = 4 and b² = 9, so a = 2 and b = 3. Area of an ellipse is πab = π(2)(3) = 6π.

questions.q: For an ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1, its area is:
questions.explanation: The standard result is Area = πab, where a and b are the semi-axis lengths. When a = b = r it reduces to the circle area πr².

questions.q: Rewriting 9x² + 4y² = 36 in standard form gives which ellipse?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 36: 9x²/36 + 4y²/36 = 1, i.e. x²/4 + y²/9 = 1. It is the same ellipse as in Q5.

questions.q: For the ellipse x²/4 + y²/9 = 1, the area of the region in the first quadrant is:
questions.explanation: By symmetry the ellipse splits into four equal quadrant regions, so first-quadrant area = (1/4)(6π) = 3π/2.

questions.q: The value of ∫ from 0 to a of (b/a)√(a² − x²) dx equals:
questions.explanation: ∫ from 0 to a of √(a² − x²) dx = πa²/4 (a quarter circle). Multiplying by b/a gives πab/4 — the first-quadrant ellipse area.

questions.q: The area under the curve y = x² from x = 0 to x = 3 is:
questions.explanation: ∫ from 0 to 3 of x² dx = [x³/3] from 0 to 3 = 27/3 = 9 square units.

questions.q: The area bounded by y = √x, the x-axis and the line x = 4 is:
questions.explanation: ∫ from 0 to 4 of √x dx = [ (2/3)x^(3/2) ] from 0 to 4 = (2/3)(8) = 16/3 square units.

questions.q: When finding the area of an ellipse by integration, why do we compute ∫ y dx and then multiply by 4?
options: Because integration only works in the first quadrant
Because the ellipse is symmetric about both axes, so all four quadrant areas are equal
Because the limits are always 0 to a
questions.explanation: The ellipse is symmetric about the x-axis and y-axis. So we find the first-quadrant area with ∫ from 0 to a of y dx and multiply by 4 to get the total.

faq.q: What is the area bounded by the ellipse x2/4 + y2/9 = 1?
faq.a: Comparing with x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 gives a = 2 and b = 3. The enclosed area is πab = π(2)(3) = 6π square units.

faq.q: Is 9x2 + 4y2 = 36 the same as x2/4 + y2/9 = 1?
faq.a: Yes. Dividing 9x² + 4y² = 36 throughout by 36 gives x²/4 + y²/9 = 1, so both equations describe the same ellipse in NCERT Ex 8.1 Q5.

faq.q: How do you set up the integral for the area of this ellipse?
faq.a: Solve for y in the first quadrant: y = (3/2)√(4 − x²). The total area is 4 times ∫ from 0 to 2 of (3/2)√(4 − x²) dx, using the symmetry of the ellipse about both axes.

faq.q: Why is the ellipse area formula pi*a*b and not pi*r squared?
faq.a: A circle is a special ellipse where a = b = r, so πab becomes πr². For a general ellipse the two semi-axes differ, and integration confirms the area is πab.
